text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:
- Tajik rebels released five more hostages on Sunday. Swiss army doctor Claude Bavaud was among them.
- Rainer Gut, chairman of Credit Suisse, said Swiss banks should not be bureaucratic about distributing money for a Holocaust memorial fond.

- Swiss prosecutors are investigating a German businessman based near Zurich on suspicion of extortion against Swiss-Swedish electrical engineering group ABB, according to the weekend newspaper SonntagsZeitung.
- Swissair pilot Peter Clausen, who was fired from his post last year for publically critizising management, may fly again for the Swiss airline.
- An international expert commission investigating the quality of human sciences in Swiss universitites gave good marks to research. However, they said there were problems recruiting young academics.
- A Geneva-based organisation urged Health Minister Ruth Dreifuss to raise the price for a packet of cigarettes to five Swiss francs from current levels around 3.70.
